traits.note: FNA vol. 27, Dicranoweisia (Schofield; efloras, read 2026-11-05): plants densely tufted, light to dark green, dull; stems 0.5-3 cm, erect, forked; leaves lanceolate, flexuose, crisped or curled when dry, 1-3.5 mm; autoicous; seta solitary, yellowish, 3-15 mm; capsule light to dark brown, elliptic to short-cylindric, 0.5-2 mm. D. cirrata (same volume): leaves crisped and incurved when dry; gemmae frequent on the leaves; capsules mature late fall to winter; short turf or tufts on tree trunks and decorticated logs, rarely in rock crevices; B.C. to California. Bryophytes at Oregon State, rooftop study (nine Willamette Valley roofs; read 2026-11-05 as summarised in a search, the site itself blocked here): Dicranoweisia cirrata very abundant (45% occurrence), Bryum capillare abundant (33%), Racomitrium canescens var. ericoides abundant but infrequent (11%), able to form large mats; Dicranoweisia and Bryum capillare the only two species found on cedar shakes; most roofs had fewer than four species.

traits.colony_form.note: FNA's dense tufts; on roofs the tufts are the neat rounded cushions that line the courses of shakes and shingles (OSU).

traits.leaf_width_m.note: Lanceolate leaves about a fifth as wide as long.

traits.capsule_posture.note: FNA gives no posture; the straight solitary seta and symmetric elliptic capsule stand erect, as in the Dicranaceae alliance.

traits.capsule_share.note: Autoicous and fruiting freely in winter (FNA, capsules mature late fall-winter); estimate.

traits.substrates.note: FNA's bark, logs and rock crevices, and roofs from OSU's survey (the commonest roof moss of western Oregon).

traits.substrate_reaction.note: Acid bark, wood and shingles; FNA names no calcareous habitat.

traits.light.note: Roofs and trunks from tree shade to open sun: the commonest moss of western Oregon roofs, thickest on north-facing parts and where trees shade them (OSU), and on trunks in forest (FNA).

traits.moisture.note: Roofs wet all winter and dry all summer west of the Cascades, and trunks and logs in forest (FNA): wet to dry.

traits.colony_spread_m_per_year.note: Estimate for a small acrocarp cushion, as Grimmia; to check against Glime, Bryophyte Ecology.

traits.leaf_colour.note: Hue measured: imagekit run moss-colour-2026-11-05 on batch moss-pnw-2026-11-05 (iNaturalist research-grade photos from Washington, about 20 a taxon, script moss_colour.py): the median linear r/g and b/g of the moss pixels (D. cirrata r/g 0.88, b/g 0.18, masked median only). Photos are exposed brighter than moss is, so only the hue is taken from them; the brightness is a green reflectance of 0.13, a lit leaf's, just above the 0.05-0.11 moss canopies reflect in the visible (Lovelock and Robinson 2002, Plant Cell Environ. 25: 1239, Antarctic Grimmia; moss biocrust albedo about 0.11 against 0.20 for bare soil, Sci. Total Environ. 2020), the canopy's own shade darkening the shell further.
